Through energy audits and upgrades, the project focused on high-impact improvements like building envelope air-sealing, light emitting diode (LED) lighting, and programmable thermostats, primarily in the Tribal Office. The initiative aimed to reduce energy waste, lower heating and electricity costs, and improve facility comfort and longevity while achieving long-term savings by decreasing reliance on imported heating oil (#1 Fuel Oil). Despite scope limitations exacerbated by budget constraints, this project achieved an approximately 47% reduction in energy use intensity (EUI) in the targeted building (the Tribal Office). Reducing operational costs emphasizes economic and environmental benefits, aligning closely with Aniak’s broader energy objectives. This initiative aligned with the Tribe’s vision for responsible energy use, addressing the challenges of high fuel oil prices in a remote community; it could serve as a model for similar efforts in Aniak and other Alaska Native villages pursuing energy
